stem: The grandfather clause in Louisiana’s 1898 constitution most directly helped white voters by

options.text: paying their poll taxes from state funds
options.misconception: The state paid white voters’ poll taxes.

options.text: exempting men whose grandfathers had voted before 1867
letting white voters cast ballots in Black precincts
options.misconception: The clause moved voters between precincts.

options.text: removing the literacy test for all voters
options.misconception: The clause ended the literacy test.

rationales.A: Background: The clause waived the tests, not the tax bill.
rationales.B: Background: the clause excused a man from the new tests if his father or grandfather could vote on or before January 1, 1867, a date before Black men could legally vote in Louisiana. White men passed through the loophole; Black men faced the tests.
rationales.C: The clause changed who had to pass the tests, not where anyone voted.
rationales.D: The literacy test stayed; the clause only excused some men from it.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what the clause waived. The literacy test and the other new requirements.
2. Ask who it waived them for. Background: men whose fathers or grandfathers voted before 1867.
3. Ask who that covers. Background: before 1867, only white men could vote in Louisiana, so the loophole favored white men.
4. Match the design. A rule that looks neutral can still sort voters by race through their grandfathers.
Remember: a grandfather clause sorts by ancestry — ask whose grandfathers could vote.

stimulus.source_note: Louisiana voter registration, 1896–1900. Figures from the Historic New Orleans Collection (64 Parishes) and the U.S. Commission on Civil Rights briefing paper, Barriers to Voting in Louisiana (2018).
stimulus.text:
| Year | Black voters registered | White voters registered |
| 1896 | 130,344 | 164,088 |
| 1898 | 12,902 | 74,133 |
| 1900 | 5,320 | 125,437 |

Source: Louisiana voter registration figures, 1896–1900. Louisiana adopted a new constitution in 1898 with a poll tax, a literacy test, a property requirement, and a grandfather clause.
